text: For a topological space X, a basis is a family B of open sets such that, whenever an open U contains x, some member of B contains x and is itself contained in U.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A subbasis for an existing topology on X is a family of open subsets whose finite intersections form a basis for that topology, with the empty intersection taken as X.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: An affine scheme is a locally ringed space isomorphic to the prime spectrum of a commutative ring equipped with its structure sheaf.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: In a category C, an object T is terminal (final) if for every object Y of C there is exactly one morphism from Y to T.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For a set A, its cardinality may be represented by the smallest ordinal equipotent to A, meaning the least ordinal for which a bijection with A exists.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: If an element alpha of an extension E/k is algebraic over k, its minimal polynomial over k is the unique monic polynomial generating the kernel of evaluation k[t] to E at alpha; it is irreducible over k.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For a nonconstant polynomial P over a field F, a splitting field is a field extension E/F in which P factors into linear terms and which is generated over F by all its roots.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A topological space is Noetherian when every descending sequence of its closed subsets eventually becomes constant.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A topological space X is quasi-compact if each open cover of X contains a finite subcollection that still covers X; no Hausdorff condition is required.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A continuous map f:X to Y is quasi-compact if the inverse image of each quasi-compact open subset of Y is quasi-compact in X.

text: For a commutative ring R, the prime spectrum Spec(R) is the set consisting of all prime ideals of R, equipped with the Zariski topology whose closed sets comprise the common zero-locus sets V(I).

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied

text: For functors L:C to D and R:D to C, L is left adjoint to R when there are bijections between the morphisms L(X) to Y in D and X to R(Y) in C, natural in both X and Y.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For an R-module M, a prime ideal p of R is associated to M if p is the annihilator ideal of some element of M.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For a field F of characteristic p greater than zero, an extension K/F is purely inseparable if, for every alpha in K, some p-power alpha^(p^n) lies in F. The trivial extension is also purely inseparable in any characteristic.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: Given morphisms B to A and B to C in a category, a pushout is an object P equipped with morphisms A to P and C to P agreeing on B, such that every other compatible pair of maps to an object T factors uniquely through P.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A morphism f:X to Y of schemes is a monomorphism when for every scheme T and two morphisms g,h:T to X, equality f composed with g = f composed with h forces g=h.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A commutative ring R is a Jacobson ring when every radical ideal I of R equals the intersection of the maximal ideals of R containing I.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied

context_hint: Infinite Galois theory: Krull topology on an absolute or relative Galois group
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For a Galois extension E/F, the Krull topology on Gal(E/F) is the weakest topology making every evaluation map sigma ↦ sigma(a), for a in E, continuous when E is discrete. With this topology the Galois group is profinite.

context_hint: Topology: constructible subset of a Noetherian space
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: If X is a Noetherian topological space, a subset C of X is constructible exactly when C can be expressed as a finite union of sets U∩F, where U is open in X and F is closed in X.

context_hint: Factorization in integral domains: associate elements
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: Two elements a and b of an integral domain R are associates if a=ub for some invertible element u of R.

context_hint: Factorization in integral domains: irreducible element
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: An element r of an integral domain R is irreducible if it is nonzero and not a unit and every factorization r=ab has at least one unit factor.

context_hint: Factorization in integral domains: prime element
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A nonzero nonunit element p of an integral domain R is a prime element when the principal ideal (p) is a prime ideal; equivalently, p divides ab only if p divides a or p divides b.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: An integral domain R is a unique factorization domain when every nonzero nonunit factors into finitely many irreducibles, and any two such factorizations agree after reordering factors and multiplying them by units.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: An integral domain R is a principal ideal domain if every ideal of R can be generated by a single element.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: ideal-factorization characterization of Dedekind domain
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: An integral domain R is a Dedekind domain in this factorization characterization if every nonzero ideal factors as a finite product of nonzero prime ideals and this decomposition is unique up to permuting the factors.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: clopen subsets of an affine spectrum
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For a commutative ring R, a subset U of Spec(R) is simultaneously open and closed exactly when there is an idempotent e of R (so e²=e) such that U=D(e)={p in Spec(R):e is not in p}; this e is unique.

context_hint: Category theory: categorically compact or finitely presentable object
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: In a category C, an object X is categorically compact if for every filtered diagram M_i whose colimit exists, the natural map colim_i Hom_C(X,M_i) → Hom_C(X,colim_i M_i) is bijective.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A strict (2,1)-category is a strict 2-category in which each 2-morphism is invertible with respect to vertical composition, so every hom-category is a groupoid.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A homomorphism of commutative rings R→S is unramified in the Stacks Project convention when S is finitely generated as an R-algebra and the module of Kähler differentials Ω_{S/R} is zero.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A ring homomorphism R→S is G-unramified in the Stacks Project convention if it is of finite presentation and Ω_{S/R}=0.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: unramified at a target prime
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For a ring map R→S and a prime ideal q in S, the map is unramified at q if some g in S outside q makes the localized map R→S_g unramified.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: G-unramified at a target prime
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For a ring map R→S and prime q of S, the map is G-unramified at q if there exists g outside q such that R→S_g is G-unramified.

context_hint: Algebra: field-valued multiplicative character of a monoid
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For a monoid G and a field L, an L-valued multiplicative character of G is a homomorphism from G to the multiplicative monoid of L; in particular it sends the identity of G to 1 and respects multiplication.

context_hint: Field theory: algebraic independence over a base field
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A family (x_i) of elements of a field extension K/k is algebraically independent over k when the evaluation homomorphism k[X_i:i∈I]→K, sending each indeterminate X_i to x_i, is injective.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: An extension K/k is purely transcendental if it is isomorphic as an extension of k to the field of rational functions in an arbitrary set of algebraically independent indeterminates over k.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A transcendence basis B of K over k is an algebraically independent subset B⊆K for which every element of K is algebraic over the subfield k(B) generated by k and B.

reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: The transcendence degree trdeg_k(K) of a field extension K/k is the cardinality of any transcendence basis of K over k, independent of the particular basis chosen.

context_hint: Field theory: relative algebraic closure inside an extension
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For a field extension K/k, the algebraic closure of k inside K is the intermediate subfield consisting of all elements of K that are algebraic over k; this is a relative, not necessarily algebraically closed, field.

context_hint: Field theory: relatively algebraically closed subfield
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: Given K/k, the base field k is algebraically closed in K when every element of K algebraic over k already belongs to k; equivalently, its relative algebraic closure in K equals k.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: flat locus of an S-module over a base ring
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: Given a ring homomorphism R→S and an S-module M, its flat locus relative to R is the subset of Spec(S) consisting of primes q for which the localization M_q is flat as an R-module, equivalently as an R_p-module for p=q∩R.

context_hint: Category theory: covariant set-valued representable functor
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A covariant functor F:C→Sets is representable if there exists an object X of C together with a natural isomorphism F(Y)≅Hom_C(X,Y) for every object Y in C.

context_hint: Set theory and algebraic geometry: cardinal size of a scheme
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: The size of a scheme S in the Stacks Project's set-theoretic convention is max(aleph_0,κ_1,κ_2), where κ_1 counts affine open subsets of S and κ_2 is the supremum of cardinalities of their rings of global sections.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: naive cotangent complex of a ring homomorphism
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For a ring map R→S, let P=R[X_s:s∈S] map canonically onto S and put I=ker(P→S). The naive cotangent complex NL_{S/R} is the two-term complex I/I²→Ω_{P/R}⊗_P S, with I/I² in homological degree 1 and the induced differential from universal derivation.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: universal homeomorphism induced by a ring map
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: A homomorphism of commutative rings R→S induces a universal homeomorphism on spectra if for every R-algebra R′ the canonical map Spec(S⊗_R R′)→Spec(R′) is a homeomorphism.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: regular Noetherian local ring
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied

text: A Noetherian local ring (R,m) of Krull dimension d is regular local if m can be generated by d elements; equivalently dim_{R/m}(m/m²)=d.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: regular system of parameters
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: In a regular Noetherian local ring (R,m) of dimension d, a regular system of parameters is a d-element sequence in m that generates the maximal ideal m.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: flat module, filtered-colimit characterization
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: An R-module M is flat if and only if M is a filtered colimit of finite-rank free R-modules; this is Lazard's equivalent characterization of the usual exactness-preservation definition of flatness.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: weakly associated prime ideal of a module
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For an R-module M, a prime ideal p of R is weakly associated to M if some element m∈M has p among the prime ideals minimal over its annihilator Ann_R(m).

context_hint: Algebraic geometry: quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine scheme
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: On X=Spec(R), a quasi-coherent O_X-module is an O_X-module isomorphic to the sheaf ~M associated with some R-module M; for every standard open D(f), the sections of ~M on D(f) identify with the localization M_f.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: I-adic completion of a ring
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For a commutative ring R and ideal I, its I-adic completion R^ is the inverse limit of the quotient rings R/I^n over positive integers n, with transition maps given by reduction modulo smaller powers.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: I-adic completion of a module
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For an R-module M and ideal I⊆R, the I-adic completion of M is lim_n M/I^n M; its elements can be viewed as mutually compatible residue classes modulo powers of I.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: I-adically complete module or ring
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: An R-module M is I-adically complete when its canonical map M→lim_n M/I^n M is an isomorphism; a ring R is I-adically complete when it has this property as its own module.

context_hint: Commutative algebra: Tor-based local criterion for module flatness
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
text: For a local map of Noetherian local rings R→S with residue field k of R and a finitely generated S-module M, M is flat over R if and only if Tor_1^R(k,M)=0.

context_hint: Field theory: finite prime field of characteristic p
reproduction_policy: independently authored paraphrase; no source passage copied
